title: Fortran Neural Network Library
description: A neural network library written in Fortran, currently a work in progress. This entry will grow alongside the implementation; architecture, supported operations, and experiments remain to be documented.

title: Computational Models of Neurons and the Brain
description: A possible direction for a future experiment: building small computational models of neurons or brain processes. No implementation or result is claimed yet; any future model would be exploratory, not a clinical method.

title: Jonas AI
description: An AI-powered German learning platform that creates personalized daily lessons from real-life situations. It combines reading, writing, and roleplay practice with instant feedback, progress tracking, and premium subscription support in a full-stack SaaS app.

title: Forge LLM: Document-Based Model Fine-Tuning
description: Built with a friend to make fine-tuning language models less of a headache. Upload PDFs, and it automatically extracts the text and generates training data from your documents, then fine-tunes models using LoRA. The whole workflow from document to trained model lives in one place.

title: Offline Wiki: RAG-Powered Knowledge Base
description: A fully offline Wikipedia/Wikivoyage search system. Ask questions about European destinations in natural language and it searches thousands of articles, using a local RAG pipeline to answer without an internet connection.

title: Jonas: Your Personal Austrian German Tutor
description: A friendly AI chatbot built as a guide to Austrian German and culture. A fine-tuned model combined with a RAG system I built with FAISS lets it explain grammar, answer questions about Austria, and chat like a local.

title: Song Popularity Predictor
description: I got curious about what makes songs popular, so I built a model to predict it. Used linear regression on Spotify data (plus synthetic variations) to see which features matter most. Simple project, fun to see what the numbers said about hit songs.

title: Malaria Cell Classifier
description: An early deep learning project classifying blood cell images as infected or uninfected with malaria using a CNN. Prepared the data, trained with binary crossentropy and Adam, and evaluated with accuracy/loss plots and a confusion matrix.

title: SimCLR from Scratch
description: A from-scratch implementation of SimCLR (Chen et al., 2020) on the HAM10000 skin lesion dataset, to understand self-supervised learning at a fundamental level. An ongoing experiment — mostly trial, error, and compute limits.

title: Klinikum Report Editor
description: A local tool to track daily wellness metrics, medication dosages, and emotional states over time. Management of mental health data with customizable fields, 9+ chart types, and privacy-preserving PDF export for healthcare providers.

title: Gmail LLM Assistant
description: A Gmail automation tool that uses a local LLM via Ollama to summarize emails and generate reply drafts. All AI processing happens locally, and drafts are reviewed before sending.

title: News Summarizer
description: An RSS news aggregator that fetches Austrian news from ORF.at, scrapes the full articles, and uses a local LLM to translate and summarize German articles into concise English. Runs entirely locally.

title: Should I Go Outside?
description: A web app that recommends outdoor activities from real-time weather, air quality, and your calendar schedule, with personalized suggestions from a local LLM.

title: Austrian Food Price Analysis
description: Compared the Producer Price Index with the Consumer Price Index for Austrian food to see how producers and consumers are affected. Cleaned and aligned the CSVs, then plotted the widening gap over time.

title: Sales Report Automation
description: Takes raw sales data and turns it into clean, multi-sheet Excel reports — revenue totals, top buyers, most cancelled items — so a manager can open a report without touching code.

title: WhatsApp Bot
description: A small WhatsApp bot built with Twilio's API to look up football scores. My first meaningful project — simple rule-based replies that solved a real problem at the time.
